site_title: dragoman: translate any page, in place
site_step_draft_detail: Bergamot, the open translation engine behind Firefox Translations, runs inside your browser. The page turns readable in about a second, and the text never leaves your computer.
site_step_refine: Refined by the model you choose
site_step_refine_detail: Paragraphs on screen go to your AI model with the page title, so names, tone and terms stay consistent. Links, bold text and formatting come back exactly where they were.
site_step_hover: The original is a hover away
site_step_hover_detail: Rest the pointer on any paragraph to read what it said before. One click on the badge, or Alt+Shift+T, puts the whole page back.
site_models_detail: Paste a key from any of these providers, or run a model on your own computer. Keys stay in your browser, and requests go straight to the provider. There is no dragoman server in between.
site_models_none: No key? On-device drafts work on their own.
site_cast_detail: For centuries, dragomans carried meaning between the Ottoman court and the rest of the world. Choose one to ride along on every page you translate.
site_languages_detail: The whole interface comes in {count} languages, from Afrikaans to isiZulu, and your AI model can translate pages into any language it knows.
site_privacy_detail: No account, no server, no analytics. Settings stay in your browser. Text goes only to the model you picked, and on-device language models download once from Mozilla.
docs_intro: Everything you need to install dragoman, connect a model and keep it running.
docs_install_2: Open helium://extensions, or chrome://extensions in other browsers, and turn on Developer mode.
docs_install_3: Choose Load unpacked and select the unzipped folder.
docs_install_4: Pin dragoman to the toolbar so it's one click away.
docs_first_detail: Open any website, click the dragoman icon, pick a language and choose Translate page. Alt+Shift+T, or Option+Shift+T on a Mac, does the same from the keyboard. Drafts appear with a dotted gold underline, which disappears as your model refines each paragraph.
docs_model_detail: Open Settings from the popup, pick a provider and follow the three steps. dragoman checks the key as soon as you paste it and preselects a fast, inexpensive model, which you can change at any time.
docs_model_openrouter: OpenRouter can create a key for you. Choose Connect with OpenRouter and approve the request.
docs_model_anthropic: Anthropic keys that aren't tied to a workspace also need a workspace ID. You'll find it in the Anthropic Console under Settings, then Workspaces.
docs_local_ollama: Install Ollama, pull a model such as gemma3, and start it with OLLAMA_ORIGINS set so it accepts requests from the extension:
docs_local_lmstudio: In LM Studio, load a model, turn on CORS in the server settings and start the local server. dragoman finds it at localhost:1234.
docs_cost_detail: dragoman is free. Refinement runs on your own key, so the provider bills you directly. Small, fast models are usually enough for translation. The Usage tab in Settings counts tokens per model each month, and turning on Show what each page costs puts the cost of the current page next to the badge.
docs_privacy_sent: What leaves your computer: the paragraphs on screen and just ahead of them, plus any text you ask your companion to translate, sent to the provider you chose, and one-time downloads of on-device language models from Mozilla. Your key is only ever sent to its own provider. dragoman has no server, no account and no analytics.
docs_help_blocked: The popup says the page can't be translated
docs_help_blocked_detail: Browser pages such as settings, the extensions page and web stores don't allow extensions to change them. Open a regular website instead.
docs_help_engine: The on-device engine has no model for this pair
docs_help_engine_detail: Bergamot covers the most widely used languages. For the rest, add an AI model and dragoman translates with it directly.
docs_help_local_detail: Check that the server is running and that its address in Settings matches. Ollama needs OLLAMA_ORIGINS, and LM Studio needs CORS turned on.
privacy_intro: dragoman has no server, no account and no analytics. This page lists everything the extension and this website do with your data.
privacy_device_local: Your settings, API keys, monthly token counts and where your companion sits are kept in your browser's extension storage. On-device translations are made inside your browser by the Bergamot engine, so the text never leaves your computer for them.
privacy_saved: dragoman also keeps the translations it makes in your browser, filed under a fingerprint of the original text, so pages you come back to appear instantly without asking the AI model again. When text changes, its fingerprint changes and it is translated fresh. Saved translations unused for 90 days are deleted, private windows save nothing, and you can clear them all under Usage in the extension settings.
privacy_detect: To name a page's language and apply your automatic translation rules, dragoman reads a short sample of each page's headings and paragraphs when it loads and passes it to your browser's built-in language detector. This also happens on your device.
privacy_sent_title: What is sent, and to whom
privacy_model_text: If you add an AI model, dragoman sends it the paragraphs on screen and a little ahead of where you are scrolling, along with the page title and the two languages. More is sent only as you scroll, or all at once if you turn on Translate the whole page at once. When you ask to translate a paragraph again, its current translation goes along so the model can do better, when you select text and choose Translate selection, only the paragraphs it touches are sent, and when you ask your companion to translate text you selected, that text is sent too. Requests go straight from your browser to the provider you chose, with your own key, and that provider's privacy policy applies. Ollama and LM Studio run on your computer, so nothing leaves it.
privacy_models: The first time you translate a language pair on the device, dragoman downloads its model from Mozilla's model storage and keeps it in your browser. These requests name only the language pair.
privacy_openrouter: Connect with OpenRouter opens OpenRouter's own sign-in page. The key it returns is stored like any other key.
privacy_never: It runs no server of its own, collects no analytics or crash reports, shows no ads, and never sells or shares your data. Each key is only ever sent to its own provider.
privacy_permissions_title: Why the extension asks for its permissions
privacy_permission_sites: Read and change your data on all websites
privacy_permission_sites_detail: Translates pages in place, and reaches the AI provider or local server you set up.
privacy_permission_storage_detail: Keeps your settings, keys, usage and saved translations on this device.
privacy_site: dragoman.io is a static site served by Cloudflare. It sets no cookies, runs no analytics and loads nothing from other services, except the launch film, which plays from YouTube in privacy-enhanced mode only after you choose to watch it. Cloudflare may keep standard request logs to run its network.
privacy_changes: If this policy changes, the new version will appear on this page with a new date.
character_envoy_detail: Carries letters between courts and speaks for both sides of the table.
character_scholar_detail: Reads seven scripts and still checks the dictionary.
offer_setting: Offer to translate pages in other languages
offer_setting_detail: When a page is in a language you don't read, the dragoman appears in the corner and asks first.
known_detail: dragoman never offers to translate pages in these languages.
known_empty: None yet. dragoman will offer to translate every page that isn't in your target language.
show_cost_detail: Shows the AI cost of the current page next to the badge and in the toolbar popup. Prices come from the provider when it reports them, otherwise from OpenRouter's public price list.
privacy_prices: If you turn on Show what each page costs, dragoman downloads OpenRouter's public list of model prices at most once a day. The request carries no page text, key or other information about you.
site_meta: A page-translation extension for Chrome, Firefox and Safari. Your device drafts every paragraph in a second, then the AI model you choose polishes it with the whole page in mind.
site_lead: dragoman translates websites right where they stand, in Chrome, Firefox and Safari, on your computer and your phone. Your device drafts every paragraph in a second, then the AI model you choose polishes it with the whole page in mind.
site_note: Free and open source. Links, photos and layout stay exactly where they were.

maker_meta: Fırat Çiftçi made dragoman, from the extension and its cast to the film and this website.
maker_say: {name}. Press to hear it said in Turkish.
maker_name_note: The draft took my name word for word: Fırat is Turkish for the Euphrates, and Çiftçi means farmer. Your model read the whole page and gave it back.
maker_intro: I have built dictionaries of Turkish, archives at the University of Chicago, and a map of every licensed dog in New York. I made dragoman, from the extension and its cast to the film and this website. I live in Brooklyn.
maker_hear: Press my name to hear it.
maker_mail_subject: Hello Fırat, dragoman brought me here
maker_river_intro: Each people on the Euphrates learned its name from the people before them and passed it on in their own tongue, the way dragomans did. Read it downstream and the names grow older, back to the Sumerians.
maker_river_signs: Akkadian and Sumerian scribes wrote the river with the same signs and read them two different ways.
maker_work_everydog: A map of all 96,459 licensed dogs in New York City, across its 197 neighborhoods.
maker_work_sozluk: The etymological dictionary of Turkish. I built and run its website, its iPhone and Android apps, and the panel its editors work in.
maker_work_yeradlari: The past and present names of 70,000 places in Turkey and its neighbors, with 77,000 older names in 34 languages.
maker_work_ottoman: The writing on more than 1,100 Ottoman buildings in Turkey, Greece and Egypt, with transliterations and photographs.
maker_shahmaran: The figure by my photo is the Shahmaran, half woman and half snake, from the folklore of Anatolia, Mesopotamia and Iran. My friend {friend} drew this one.
meaning_lead: Dragomans were the interpreters, translators and guides who carried words between the Ottoman court and the embassies, consulates and trading posts of Europe. They had to know Turkish, Arabic and Persian, as well as the languages of Europe.
meaning_quote: The tongue that speaks, the ear that hears.
meaning_quote_by: A Venetian ambassador in the 1700s, on his dragomans
meaning_word: The word itself went from tongue to tongue.
meaning_fact_porte: The first Dragoman of the Sublime Porte, Panagiotis Nikousios, was Greek, and most of the princes who ruled Wallachia and Moldavia from 1711 to 1821 had held the same office.
meaning_fact_tax: Dragomans were exempt from taxes, and embassy dragomans often met Ottoman officials without their ambassador in the room.
meaning_fact_office: In the Tanzimat era, the Translation Office of the Sublime Porte became one of the surest roads to power in the Ottoman government.
model_overview: dragoman translates on your device out of the box. Add an AI model for more natural translations that use the whole page as context. Your key stays in this browser, and requests go straight to the provider.
provider_none_info: Translates on your device, quickly and privately. No account needed.

usage_none: Nothing yet. Pages translated by an AI model show up here.
saved_translations_detail: Translations stay on this device, so pages you come back to appear instantly without asking the AI model again. Text that changes is translated fresh, anything unused for 90 days is removed, and private windows save nothing.

pet_morning: Good morning! Coffee first, then languages.
pet_afternoon: Good afternoon! Any pages that need an interpreter?
pet_evening: Good evening. The lamps are lit and the dictionaries are open.
pet_night: Still up? Even the palace interpreters slept sometimes.
pet_start_3: One moment, sharpening my reed pen.
pet_done: Done! Hover over any paragraph to see the original.
pet_done_touch: Done! Tap any paragraph to see the original.
pet_dizzy: Whoa… I see two of you. Very bilingual.
pet_wake: I wasn't asleep. I was conjugating.
pet_end: That's the end of the page.
pet_stumped: That one stumped me. Try a shorter piece?
pet_fact_name: My title comes from the Akkadian targumannu, “interpreter”. It traveled through Aramaic, Arabic and Turkish to reach you.
pet_fact_porte: Dragomans of the Sublime Porte translated treaties, letters and the occasional royal insult. Very politely.
pet_fact_count: About 7,000 languages are spoken today. I'm working on it.
pet_fact_coffee: A Turkish saying: a cup of coffee is remembered for forty years.
pet_fact_two: An old saying: one language, one person; two languages, two people.
pet_fact_rosetta: The Rosetta Stone says the same thing three times. Interpreters call that a good start.
pet_fact_look: Yaghan is said to have mamihlapinatapai: a look between two people who each hope the other will make the first move.
pet_fact_carry: Some words don't travel. Then I carry the meaning instead.
pet_idle_1: I'm right here if you need a word.
pet_idle_3: Every page is a little journey.
